title: NAM per-unit attribution: pruning low-contribution units does NOT improve omitted-identity decoding

claims.statement: jnwb/nam.py's grouped-operation NAM recovers a known set of informative units and their attribution ordering.
claims.receipt: Synthetic case (N=20 units, T=21, n=600, ONLY units 4/9/15 carrying class information, other 17 pure noise): balanced test accuracy 1.0 vs 0.333 chance; top-3 units by importance exactly [4,9,15]; mean S 2.055 informative vs 0.151 noise. Run 2026-08-07.

claims.statement: Ranking units by NAM attribution on a held-out validation split and pruning the low-contribution tail does NOT improve test decoding of omitted identity. The hypothesis that low-trial-count units acquire weights that actively hurt classification is TESTED AND NOT SUPPORTED on this corpus.
claims.receipt: outputs/classification/fig04_v9_nam_{spikes,lfp}.csv, 21 sessions, 60/59 cells, px window, 40/30/30 split with prune level selected on VAL and read once on TEST. Spikes: mean prune gain -0.0011, 28/60 cells improved (binomial p=0.699, 95% CI 0.337-0.600), Wilcoxon on gain p=0.746. LFP: mean gain -0.0007, 22/59 improved (binomial p=0.067, CI 0.250-0.509), Wilcoxon p=0.606. Coin-flip in both.
claims.note: The selection was made on VAL, never TEST. Had the prune level been chosen on TEST, a positive gain would have been guaranteed by construction regardless of signal -- that is why this is a real test.

claims.statement: The NAM finds no population of near-zero-contribution LFP channels to discard: 0.0% of channels fall below 5% of the max attribution, corpus-wide. For spikes the figure is 12.2%.
claims.receipt: Same files, importance_frac_near_zero column, mean over 59 (LFP) and 60 (spikes) cells.

claims.statement: The NAM, a strictly more expressive model than the bilinear or flatten+PCA decoders, lands in the same near-chance band: balanced accuracy 0.368 (spikes) and 0.350 (LFP) vs 0.333 chance.
claims.blocked_on: Permutation null (fig04_v8) still running. Stays unconfirmed until an empirical null exists for this statistic.

issues: Four model classes (1D scalar, flatten+PCA 2D, bilinear 2D, NAM) now agree on a near-chance result for omitted identity, while every positive control decodes cleanly. Convergent negative, pending the null.
Not built, not requested: temporal cross-generalization (T x T), sliding-window p_A(t) curves, layer-wise decoders.
falsifier: Pruning claim closed: pre-registered direction (gain > 0) tested on held-out test data with val-only selection, result is coin-flip in both modalities.
